newsitem.title: USA: Carter-Wallace says CPI not to sell shares.
newsitem.headline: Carter-Wallace says CPI not to sell shares.

text.p: Carter-Wallace Inc said on Tuesday the CPI Development Corp, which owns an absolute majority of Carter-Wallace common stock, told the company it had no interest in selling shares under the Davis Companies offer.
Investor Marvin Davis and his Davis Companies raised a bid for Carter-Wallace, which makes Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorant, to $20 per share from $18 per share on November 18.
Carter-Wallace said, given CPI's position, it had decided not to take any more action regarding the Davis proposal.

CPI Development is a personal holding company with three members -- Carter-Wallace Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Henry Hoyt Jr., Hoyt's sister Suzanne Garcia and Richard Cruess, who was on Carter-Wallace's board of directors, a company spokesman said.
Cruess is a professor of surgery at the Center for Medical Education at Canada's McGill University, he said.
